I'm going to play devil's advocate for a second.

He says that others say that without the government the poor will not be protected by courts.
He says that currently the poor fear the courts now more than common criminals.

My devil's advocacy is that this is the wrong way to look at it from an optimization stand point. I still agree with getting rid of the state on grounds of lacking moral authority but he is making an optimization argument and that's not how the math works.

It is possible as the people he refers to might argue that under no government criminals would be more dangerous and the and the government less so. So then under his own argument that would call for a state. If you follow the pattern it regresses to an equal fear of state and criminal. Is that the correct math? No.

From an optimization stand point you would want the margins of increased fear set equal to each other for government and criminal per unit of increased or decreased government.

 

The question is if we made the government half as scary would we see the increased fear of criminals make up the gap. I don't think so. Even if criminals were twice as scary because government invokes greater terror in the poor than criminals, that still is a reduction in terror for the poor even with criminals being twice as scary.

Would criminals be twice as scary if government reduced it's abuse in half? I don't think so, and that is the threshold we would need to meet before the decision becomes unclear at all. Criminals typically have mental issues (all people have mental issues). They do not respond to rules or fear the same as other people. In fact increased fear can make them rationalize more violence. Then the other question is if assinine rules have anything to do with reducing criminal behavior that causes terror in others, at all. Generally no, and these are the things people really fear. You get very little bang for buck with the state. Nobody feels terror over others breaking copyright law. Your terror reduced for terror produced is 1:100. That is a doubling the number of rules doesn't yield half the crime just about ever (and it would have to go well beyond that because of partial derivatives). We need a 3:1 ratio, not a 1:100.

So that's the measure for if the government is producing a product. I still don't see the moral authority for them to produce a product for me, via often arbitrary abuse of others. Stealing a phone has value to me, that doesn't make it right. But it is really sad when the product they offer, which they have no authority to produce, has negative value and it's mandatory.
